answer: The protocol refuses to accept new stake beyond 35% of the pool from any one declared operator, so anyone cannot buy dominance outright. Because the beacon declaration is reconciled against the copper funding graph, the delta audit exposes a hidden operator and its excess is returned without reward. Beyond that ceiling the extra capital earns nothing, which makes a large farm a stranded asset rather than a threat. That is 21 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
